title: 禪宗頌古聯珠通集 (Anthology of Chan Verse Commentaries on Koans, 40 juan)
shelf_note: The Song-Yuan anthology of verse commentaries (songgu) on Chan cases, compiled by Faying and continued by Puhui; core Chan literature.
structure_note: Library of Congress two-leaf spreads of a Ming woodblock. printed_backsteps 67 / printed_repeats 165 are what you expect from leaf numbers that restart in every juan and two leaves per image, not a splice. The colophon on p.836 (萬曆丁酉 = 1597) matches the catalogue date. 952/956 pages OCR'd, 938-950 translated.
reader_summary: This is the real Lianzhu tongji, in a 1597 woodblock edition. The verse pages are transcribed closely and the English reads as an honest literal rendering. But on the denser pages, single misread characters change who speaks and what is meant: 觜 is read as 背, 陷 is dropped, a place name is swapped. On p.836 the printer's colophon box is left out entirely, and a lineage note names the wrong ancestor.

title: 石門文字禪·卷二十九~卷三十 (vol 11)
shelf_note: Juan 29-30 of Juefan Huihong's Shimen wenzi chan (letters, a stele biography, sacrificial texts); Song Chan literature.
structure_note: A Siku quanshu (欽定四庫全書) manuscript copy, photographically reproduced, from the Internet Archive universallibrary set. '1773' is the Siku date, not the work's (Huihong d.1128). printed_backsteps 8 are where juan 29 gives way to juan 30, and leaf numbers restart. Not a defect.
reader_summary: This is Huihong's collected prose in the Siku copy. Three of four pages are transcribed accurately, and the English is careful and readable. On p.45 the transcription drops a line and a half and turns 過焉仁曰 into a temple called 'Ma-ren'. The English then puts Yangshan in the narrator's dining hall and has the narrator ask Guishan's question.

title: Jikji (직지심체요절, Anthology of Great Buddhist Priests' Zen Teachings)
shelf_note: The 1377 Korean anthology of Chan sayings (BnF, the surviving second volume).
structure_note: Gallica copy of the surviving volume 2 (下), so the book begins mid-text. Last record (p.86) is the spine, not a text page. 82 of 86 translated.
reader_summary: This is the BnF Jikji itself, the 1377 metal-type print, and the transcription follows its leaves closely. But on p.28 it drops the key line of Dongshan's river verse (渠今正是我). The English is literal and mostly right. It slips where names hide in the text: 文邃 becomes 'you, a fellow seeker', and 點胷 becomes 'reflected'. A note calls the printed book a 'manuscript'.

ocr_errors.problem: Wensui's name misread and 箇 dropped
胷 'chest' read as 肯; the gesture (pointing to his chest) is lost

tr_errors.problem: Xuefeng blames his former companion Wensui; the English makes Yantou the burden

tr_errors.english: The master himself reflected and said
tr_errors.problem: carries the misread; should be 'pointed to his own chest'

tr_errors.problem: the English half-restores the dropped line from memory and reverses the order, so the two panes disagree

tr_errors.problem: Yunyan was Dongshan's teacher (和尚 'Venerable')

tr_errors.source: 竟觀機關木人修道何時得達彼岸

tr_errors.problem: phrase split wrongly: 'a mechanical wooden man cultivating the Way: when will it reach the other shore?'

ocr_errors.image: spine with about four partly legible characters
ocr_errors.problem: full catalogue title supplied where the spine shows fewer, partly illegible characters

other.note: OCR and translation call the Jikji a 'manuscript'; it is the 1377 movable metal-type print (the reason it is famous)

book_verdict: The genuine Jikji, transcribed leaf by leaf, with readable English. On p.28 the most quoted line of Dongshan's verse is missing from the transcription, and names inside sentences get misread. It needs a caveat before a scholar sees it.

title: 六祖大師法寶壇經 (Platform Sutra of the Sixth Patriarch)
shelf_note: The Zongbao-recension Platform Sutra; core Chan scripture.
structure_note: 44 pages, all OCR'd and translated, sequence continuous across the four sampled pages. Only one page carries a printed number (it is born-digital). The edition the transcription comes from is not named.
reader_summary: This is the standard (Zongbao) Platform Sutra as a modern typed text, not an old edition. The transcription is near perfect and the English is a faithful, readable translation. The caveat is the source: a scholar sees an anonymous modern typescript with no named edition. One note invents a 'rival school' behind the plot to steal Huineng's head.

tr_errors.english: <note>…by a monk hired by a rival school…</note>
tr_errors.problem: the note invents a 'rival school'; the traditional account is Zhang Jingman hired by the Korean Kim Daebi

book_verdict: Clean text and a trustworthy translation of the standard Platform Sutra. But the source is an anonymous modern typescript, not a historical edition, and it should be labelled as such.
